content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a polished bookmark manager called **Kept**.

Features include:

- Add and edit bookmarks
- Search across titles, domains, notes, tags, and collections
- Favorites, unread, and archive views
- Grid and list layouts
- Sorting controls
- Local browser persistence
- Responsive mobile navigation
- Helpful empty states and notifications

The production build passes successfully and the application is available at:

**http://maker:4000**

This looks really lovely — clean, easy to read, and the favorites/read-later/archive views and search all feel natural. A couple of things stop it short of what I need before I'd call it done, though:

1. **Saving is more work than I expected.** When I paste in a web address, I want it to go fetch the page's title and description (and its little icon) for me automatically, so I usually don't have to type anything. Right now I have to fill in the title and the note myself — if I leave the title blank it just uses the web address. Grabbing that info for me is a big part of why I wanted this.

2. **I can't actually delete a bookmark.** The menu only lets me edit or move something to the archive. Archiving is great for tucking things away, but I also need a way to get rid of a bookmark for good when I'm sure I don't want it. Those should be two different things.

One smaller thing while you're in there: when I see a tag on a bookmark, I'd expect to be able to click it and see everything else with that same tag.

The rest — search, the different views, sorting, the layouts — feels good enough for how I'll use it. If you can sort out the automatic page info and a real delete, I think this will be there.

content:
Implemented and verified all three improvements:

- Pasting a URL now automatically fetches its page title and description. Favicons are derived from the detected domain.
- Added permanent deletion with a confirmation dialog, separate from archive and restore.
- Tags are clickable and open a filtered view; the active tag can be cleared from the toolbar.
- Metadata failures fall back gracefully to manual entry without blocking saving.
- Confirmed the production build and browser interactions work.

Updated app: **http://maker:4000**

That's exactly what I was hoping for. I tried adding a bookmark and it filled in the title and description from the page on its own, and when a page didn't cooperate it just let me type it in myself instead of getting stuck. Deleting now really removes something for good, with a clear warning, and it's nicely separate from archiving and restoring. And clicking a tag pulls up everything with that tag, which I can clear again from the top.

That covers everything I needed. Saving is easy now, and I can properly tidy up my collection. I'm happy with it — thank you.
